title: Module 4: D minor, finger stretches, and strumming refinements
summary: In this JustinGuitar module (Lesson 4), the instructor introduces a new D minor chord, presents a finger-stretching exercise to aid chord reach, and delves into strumming technique—including how to miss a down strum and how to stay in time with a common strumming pattern. He also covers practical setup adjustments such as keeping fingernails short and choosing the right pick for different tasks, with specific references to tortex (orange) picks, nylon thin picks, and thicknesses around 0.46–0.60 mm. The segment concludes by signaling that the finger-stretching exercise will be revisited in the next lesson.

sections.title: Module 4 Introduction
sections.description: Discussion of how missing a down strum feels, and the relevance of practicing a widely used strumming pattern.

sections.title: Tip 1: Keep your fingernails short
sections.description: Guidance to keep fingernails short to avoid interference with the fretboard and fretting hand; tips on trim levels and avoiding contact with wood.

sections.title: Tip 2: Get the RIGHT Pick
sections.description: Detailed discussion of choosing picks for different tasks: very thin nylon picks for strumming, a medium-thickness pick for finger exercises, and slightly thicker picks for later practice. Specific examples include orange tortex as a commonly used medium pick and 0.60 mm nylon vs 0.46 mm nylon as comparative thicknesses to influence control and feel.
